A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CEBE/CSE research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–G. Relocated material, including the checklist, and renumbered displays can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original Cliffwalking approximation experiments and reinforcement-learning evaluations on SimpleDirection, classic-control, and MuJoCo environments, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds automatic-differentiation and stochastic-environment evaluations, plus aggregate analysis in Appendix C.4–C.6.

M1.justification: The CEBE definitions, CSE augmentation rule, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Automatic differentiation supplies the same required gradients in an additional experiment; no new algorithmic component, objective, or architecture is introduced.

E1.justification: Appendix C.5 adds SimpleDirection-Stochastic, with Gaussian noise affecting transitions and rewards. The original task suite remains. PendulumGoal-AD changes gradient computation without establishing a distinct task or domain.

E2.justification: The retained experiments use the same baseline SAC or DQN and local domain randomization comparators. New Figures 8–9 likewise compare SAC, SAC+CSE, and SAC+LDR; no comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Additional experiments use automatic gradients and per-step noise specified as N(0, 0.1). Appendix C.6 introduces averaging across context sweeps and a normalized performance metric. Existing training budgets, architectures, and hyperparameter tables are retained; the one-step-return statement is newly disclosed information.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4–C.6 substantially broadens supplementary analysis beyond the retained context sweeps: it tests automatic-gradient implementation, robustness to stochastic transitions and rewards, and the relationship between aggregate performance and context dimension. The dimension analysis is exploratory rather than a controlled scaling experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 10 trained policies, evaluation over 64 trajectories, and means with 95% confidence intervals. No revised repetition counts, seed information, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported. The new aggregate table supplies point estimates without additional uncertainty analysis.

E6.justification: Existing result plots are unchanged. New Figures 8–9 report performance with automatic gradients and added noise, generally showing CSE comparable to LDR. New Table 1 aggregates earlier sweeps: CSE exceeds baseline in all six environments and LDR in three. These are additional results, not improvements to the retained results.

T1.justification: Appendix C.6 newly defines the normalized score (CSE − Baseline)/(LDR − Baseline). This is a limited mathematical-definition addition; the CMDP assumptions, Theorems 1–4, appendix proofs, and worked derivations remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about first-order CEBE approximation, CSE augmentation, and improved generalization from limited training contexts. The additional evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the noisy experiment as empirical robustness evidence while explicitly leaving theoretical guarantees open. It adds qualifications about confounding in the context-dimension comparison and potential error accumulation with multi-step returns, alongside broader applicability to algorithms using bootstrapping.

D1.justification: The anonymous code-access link is replaced by a named GitHub repository link. Appendix D explicitly discloses one-step returns for SAC and DQN, and Appendix C.4 identifies automatic gradient computation. Existing hardware and hyperparameter information is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds four domain-randomization references and discusses Zhao et al. (2024) in Appendix A, distinguishing its discrete hierarchical approach from continuous-context training. Other changes largely update bibliographic information for existing works, including the meta-RL survey and RLlib Flow.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and terminology edits, adds acknowledgments and short experimental subsections, and updates affiliation and conference text. The checklist moves after the appendices, while the scientific narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 8–9 and an aggregate-results table. It resizes and repositions Figure 1, relocates several existing displays, and clarifies the Figure 3 caption. Original plots are retained; existing tables and the Cliffwalking illustration are renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added automatic-gradient and noise tests provide useful practical validation missing from v1, while aggregate results and explicit one-step-return disclosure improve interpretability and reproducibility. The gains remain limited, and an inconsistency persists: Table 1 reports AntGoal CSE at −2307.24 versus LDR at −2157.52, despite Appendix C.3 retaining the claim that CSE performs at least as well across all contexts.
